results.note: Nicolaus Claraevallensis, secretary to Bernard of Clairvaux. No English translation of this preface fragment located.
Sermon on feast of St. Stephen by Nicholas of Clairvaux. No English translation found despite searches for sermon collections.
Sermon on feast of St. Andrew by Nicholas of Clairvaux. No English translation located.
Sermon on feast of St. Nicholas of Myra by Nicholas of Clairvaux. No English translation found.
Sermon on the Nativity of Christ by Nicholas of Clairvaux. No English translation located.
Letters of Nicholas of Clairvaux (23.7K words). No comprehensive English translation found; letters survive but not translated to English.
Notker Balbulus, 'On the Interpreters of Scripture.' No English translation located despite searches for Notker's scholarly works.
Notker Balbulus, 'De musica.' Notker known for musical work (Liber Hymnorum) but this specific treatise's translation status unclear.
Brief epistola to Ruodpertus (233 words). No English translation found despite general availability of other Notker correspondence.
Notker Balbulus, 'Formulae' (1.6K words, liturgical formulas). No English translation located.
Notker Balbulus, 'Martyrologium' (49.9K words). No specific English translation found; this large calendar work exists in Latin but translation status ambiguous.

Notker Balbulus, 'Sequentiae.' Contained in The Liber Ymnorum of Notker Balbulus (Henry Bradshaw Society, 2016), translated by Calvin M. Bower. Volume II provides English translations of the 49 sequences. Won Palisca Prize 2017.
Theodulf of Orleans, 'Capitula ad presbyteros' (first capitulary, 6K words). Influential capitulary mentioned in scholarly literature but no published English translation located.
Theodulf of Orleans, 'Capitulare ad eosdem' (second capitulary, 5.8K words). Known work on penance but no published English translation found.

Theodulf of Orleans, 'Carmina' (poetry collection, 27.8K words). Translated by Theodore M. Andersson et al., Medieval and Renaissance Texts and Studies 450 (Arizona Center for Medieval and Renaissance Studies, 2014). Also earlier Alexandrenko translation (1970).
Theodulf of Orleans, 'De Spiritu Sancto' (14.8K words, theological treatise on Filioque). Theological importance noted but no English translation located.
Theodulf of Orleans, 'De ordine baptismi' (6.5K words). No English translation located despite liturgical significance.
Theodulf of Orleans, 'Fragmenta sermonum' (2.4K words). No English translation found.
Urban II, 'De Dalmachio promoto in episcopum Compostellae' (147 words, brief text on promotion to bishopric). No English translation located.

Urban II, 'Epistolae et privilegia' (91.1K words). English translations available on Wikisource (e.g., letter to Bologna, Sept 19 1096), based on Edward Peters (2011) translation and Georg Strack (2016) commentary.
Urban II, 'Epitaphium Simonis' (75 words). Very brief epitaph; no English translation located.
Urban II, 'Epitaphium duplex' (100 words, double epitaph). No English translation found.
Urban II, 'Privilegium ecclesiae Matisconensis' (123 words, church privilege). No English translation located.

Urban II, 'Sermones' (7.3K words). Versions of Urban's sermons (notably the Clermont sermon of 1095) available in English translation via Wikisource and other medieval sourcebooks, though paraphrased through chronicler accounts.
Adémar de Chabannes, 'Acrostichon ad Rohonem' (285 words, acrostic poem). No English translation located.

Adémar de Chabannes, 'Commemoratio abbatum Lemovicensium' (1.9K words, history of abbots of Saint-Martial). Partial English translation available on 'The Historians' Sketchpad' blog (salutemmundo.wordpress.com, 2023), free online access.
Adémar de Chabannes, 'Epistola de apostolatu S. Martialis' (9.3K words, on the apostolate of St. Martial). Important hagiographic letter but no published English translation located.
Adémar de Chabannes, 'Fragmentum Sermonis in Concilio Lemovicensi' (364 words, sermon fragment from Council of Limoges). No English translation found.
Adémar de Chabannes, 'Historiae' (14.1K words, three-book chronicle). No comprehensive English translation located; this major work survives in Latin but is not translated to English.
Pope Adrian I, 'Bulla' (406 words, papal bull). No English translation located.
Pope Adrian I, 'Capitula' (3.7K words). No English translation found despite Adrian's importance to Charlemagne's reign.
Pope Adrian I, 'Epistola metrica' (271 words, metrical letter). No English translation located.

Pope Adrian I, 'Epistolae' (15K words, letters to Charlemagne, preserved in Codex Carolinus). Latin letters well-studied in scholarship; English translation status ambiguous—fragments quoted in scholarly works but comprehensive English translation unclear.
Pope Adrian I, 'Epistola' (21.6K words, large letter from vol. 98). Status unclear; likely same as 3530 (Codex Carolinus correspondence) but translation availability not confirmed.

Auctor incertus (Hugo de S. Victore?), 'De VII vitis et VII donis' (1.1K words, on seven vices and seven gifts). Attribution uncertain; if by Hugh of Saint Victor, may have translation in Brepols collections, but specific work not confirmed.

Auctor incertus (Hugo de S. Victore?), 'De substantia dilectionis' (1.8K words, on the substance of love). If by Hugh of Saint Victor, included in 'On love: a selection of works of Hugh, Adam, Achard, Richard and Godfrey of St Victor' (Brepols, 2011, ed. Hugh Feiss). Free access via academic publishers.
Auctor incertus (Hugo de S. Victore?), 'Posteriores excerptiones' (114.9K words, very large collection of excerpts). Questionable attribution; no translation found despite size.
Auctor incertus (Hugo de S. Victore?), 'De modo dicendi et meditandi' (1.3K words, on manner of speaking and meditating). Uncertain attribution; no translation located.
Auctor incertus (Hugo de S. Victore?), 'Miscellanea' (173K words, large miscellaneous collection). Very large work with uncertain attribution; no translation found.
Auctores incerti, 'Hymni' (8K words, anonymous medieval hymns). Medieval hymns often translated (John Mason Neale, etc.) but these specific works not identified in searches.
Auctores incerti, 'Graeca fragmenta libri nominum Hebraicorum' (7.7K words, Greek fragments on Hebrew names). No English translation located.
Auctores incerti, 'Liturgica' (4.3K words, anonymous liturgical text). Medieval liturgical texts sometimes translated but this specific text not identified.
Auctores incerti, 'Chronici S. Benigni continuatio' (4.6K words, continuation of St. Benignus chronicle). No English translation found despite searches for medieval chronicles.
Auctores incerti, 'Chronicon S. Benigni Divionensis' (35K words, Chronicle of Saint Benignus of Dijon). Medieval chronicle; no English translation located despite its significant length.
